Aloha Social connects your Nextcloud account to the Fediverse through the ActivityPub standard.

What it does:
- 🧭 Timelines: home, local, global (federated), direct messages, liked posts, notifications, hashtags
- 🏷️ For you: a feed made of the hashtags you read, learned from what you stay on, skip, like, boost and watch, also for photos, videos and Shorts, with a tag cloud in the settings to reorder, pin, add and remove them. Private, never federated, and switchable to opt-in by the administrator
- ✍️ Posts: write posts and replies with a visibility setting, mentions, hashtags, content warnings and media attachments
- ✏️ Edit and delete your own posts; edits are federated as ActivityPub Update activities
- 👍 🔁 💬 Like, boost and reply
- 👥 Follow and unfollow local and remote accounts; incoming follows are accepted automatically unless the account is locked
- 🔎 Find accounts and hashtags via WebFinger and search
- 🌐 Federation: signed delivery of ActivityPub activities, with a delivery queue processed by cron
- 📊 Dashboard tiles for mentions, direct messages, your timeline, bookmarks, follow requests and trending hashtags, plus open reports and federation health for administrators
- 🔒 Photos have their Exif metadata — including the coordinates a phone writes into them — removed before they are stored or federated
- 🎬 A Videos timeline, including the videos from PeerTube channels anyone here follows: streamed from the instance that holds them rather than copied here, and proxied so no viewer's address reaches a server they never chose
- 📡 Videos posted here federate as ActivityPub Video objects filed under a channel, which is what PeerTube needs before it will take one at all, with a poster frame, byte-range seeking and a 2 GB ceiling of their own
- ▶️ A video opens on a watch page: its title, the channel with a Subscribe button, its chapters as links that seek, and where you stopped offered back as continue watching. Every channel and account has an RSS feed with an enclosure per video
- 🪜 An administrator can have each stored video written at a ladder of smaller sizes as HLS, so a player picks what the connection carries; and can set a per-account video quota, see who is holding the disk, choose what happens to media marked sensitive, and hold every post with a video for a moderator
- 📥 A channel can be brought over from PeerTube's own export, or a single video by its address
- 🎨 Filters in the composer and a profile that draws as a grid
- 🗂️ Collections, 24-hour shorts and places
- 📱 Pixelfed's own routes — the config its app reads on launch, discover, the story carousel, collections, mutuals, reports, direct-message threads, push (honestly off) and its admin screens — so its app finds what it looks for once the API is at the domain root
- 🖼️ Shorts, collections and places in the web app: a Shorts bar above your feed with the people whose 24-hour shorts are up, one player for every short and a way to post one; albums as the fourth tab of a profile, each a page of its posts; a pin in the composer that says where a picture was taken, and a page for every place — with nothing ever sent to a map service
- 🧭 A Discover page: who to follow, with starter packs you can follow in one go, and the people your follows follow drawn as a constellation you can drag around and follow from
- 🎲 A composer that plays: /dice, /flip and /pick are rolled when the post goes out and sent as plain text, a short post can go out as a card drawn on colour, and a new post makes an entrance at the top of the timeline
- ✨ 24-hour shorts as words on a coloured card, or a picture with stickers dragged onto it — both drawn into the picture, so they arrive elsewhere as you made them
- ❤️ Hearts on the video stack: a like button, and double tap to like with a heart where your finger was
- 🎥 Shorts, kept or for 24 hours: keep a short on your profile, or post one for your followers only that is gone after a day and goes to Pixelfed too. The Shorts stack plays the 24-hour shorts of the people you follow first; its composer asks how long a short lasts, then lets you upload, drop or record a video with a countdown, trim it, pick its cover frame, add trending hashtags and choose who can watch
- 🔊 Sound and touch, per device: a tick on a like, a chime for a direct message, a tap in the hand on a phone. Sound is off until you turn it on; Shorts play with sound, or muted with "Tap for sound" where the browser will not start it
- 📤 Share to Aloha Social from the Files app: pick pictures or videos there and the composer opens with them attached
- 👥 Lists, and the Nextcloud groups an administrator chooses as lists of their own — kept in step with the group automatically; you make, rename, delete and fill your own in Settings
- ⚙️ Account settings: the name you publish under, whether people ask before they follow you, whether other servers may suggest you and index your public posts, and the audience every new post starts with
- 🔗 The profile editor says which of your fields are verified links, and gives you the line to paste on your own site to earn the tick
- 👋 A short introduction on the first visit: your address, who to follow, and a way to bring the follows you already have
- 📱 A layout for phones: the post takes the width of the screen, the face inside the card, the composer's toolbar wrapping
- 🔗 Links that land where they should: a post or profile link opens inside the app when you are signed in, a search can be reloaded or sent to somebody, and an address that names nobody says so instead of erroring
- 🩺 For administrators: setup checks in Administration → Overview — WebFinger, the address ids are built from, the delivery job, the outbound queue, whether Mastodon apps can reach the API and whether there is a memory cache — and a Server card for the instance settings that used to need occ
- 🔗 A link to a post or a profile here unfurls into a card in Talk, Text and Deck
- 🕘 Follows, mentions, boosts and favourites show in the Activity app too, and in its digest mail for those who turn that on
- 🗓️ A composer that says what a post is: the language it is written in, a clock to publish it later (with the waiting posts listed in Settings), and a crosshair that says where the subject of a picture is
- 😀 Emoji reactions on a post, federated as EmojiReact, with the faces behind each one
- 💬 Quote posts, carrying the original author's permission on the wire
- 😀 Custom emoji of this instance's own, added with occ social:emoji and rendered on servers that have never seen them
- 🎞️ A GIF picker in the composer, backed by the instance's own library rather than a third party
- 📈 Your own statistics: the last 30 days beside the 30 before them — reach, interactions, likes and boosts, each with the percentage it moved by — then every post of the window one by one, what works, when to post and where your followers are. A statistics page for the instance too, and profile highlights showing what somebody posts about
- 🕰️ On this day, and a weekly recap of what you missed
- 📣 Announcements: what the administrators of this instance are telling everybody, at the top of the timeline until it is read, dismissed once for every device, with an emoji to say something back
- 📡 Relays: subscribe to one and a new server's federated timeline stops being empty — a relay rebroadcasts the public posts of every server on it and carries this server's public posts out to all of them. Public posts only, and a relayed post arrives as the post it is rather than as a boost by the relay
- 💬 Quote controls: who may quote each of your posts (anybody, your followers, nobody), who already has, and a button that detaches one and tells their server
- 🔑 Authorized apps: every app holding a key to your account, with what it may do and when it was last used, and a button that signs one out — the page to open after losing a phone
- 🚪 Delete your Aloha Social account from Settings and keep your Nextcloud one: the posts, the follows, and a Delete to every server that knew you
- 🔕 Filtered notifications: the senders your notification policy is holding, one row each, with Show these and Dismiss — and a way to hide a whole server rather than its accounts one at a time
- 📜 Edit history: the "Edited" line under a post opens every version of it
- 🧳 Migration in both directions: move in from another server from nothing but your old handle (it is followed over and your posts are brought along, in the background); the blocks, mutes and lists another network exported, read here; and your follows, followers, blocks, mutes and lists written back out one CSV at a time, the way Mastodon writes them
- 📅 Your year, as a report — Mastodon's #Wrapstodon, through the API (the web client has no page for it yet): twelve months of what you posted and who arrived, the hashtags you used, the three posts that travelled furthest
- 🛡️ For moderators: what may trend (a hashtag, a link or a post kept out of Explore), the instance's custom emoji and its rules, all from the administration page rather than from occ

You can pin your own posts to the top of your profile, bookmark any post, and see which hashtags the instance is using most. How many likes, boosts and followers things have is hidden unless you turn the numbers on, in the web app and in your Mastodon apps alike. This is a partial implementation of ActivityPub and of the Mastodon client API. Blocking, muting and reporting (with a moderation panel in the administration settings) are supported, as are locked accounts with approvable follow requests. Polls are fully supported: create your own, and view and vote on federated ones. Profiles carry an avatar, a banner image and up to four profile metadata fields, edited in the profile editor; a field naming a web page is marked as verified once that page links back with rel="me". Posts that link somewhere get a link preview card. Image (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, and HEIC from an iPhone where the server can read it), video (MP4, WebM, QuickTime) and audio attachments are supported, up to ten per post, each with alt text and a focal point; where the server has ffmpeg, QuickTime and HEVC videos are converted to H.264 MP4, and a new post waits up to ten minutes for that before it is sent, so that other servers accept its video. Quote posts carry the original author's permission on the wire, and the author decides who may quote each post and can take one back afterwards. Mastodon apps work once the web server maps /api and /oauth at the domain root onto the app — the rules ship in contrib/webserver/ and Administration → Overview says whether they are in place; there is no streaming API and no push subscriptions. A post can be translated where this Nextcloud has a translation provider. An administrator can let a limited number of people without an account register one that reaches Aloha Social only, from a button on the login page: by invitation, with approval, or openly, with a media quota and optional two-factor enforcement.

Settings → Account → Download your data. The archive holds your videos as files rather than as posts, so there is nothing here that can read it as a timeline yet.
